candidates.title: Count scheduled order differences

demandEvidence.chore: A scheduled run is starting itself; the post title frames it as a daily count check for missing, extra and mismatched orders.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The Schedule Trigger started every run itself (one-off cron a few seconds ahead).

ease.reason: A sample row set can be counted; n8n Summarize documents total and unique counts, not scheduling or matching.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: professional service operators reconciling orders might pay; one discussion does not establish payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week demo can count operator-supplied rows, but identifying missing or mismatched orders and scheduling are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A proposed scheduled report could repeat; a person must validate the data and resolve discrepancies, and schedule support is undocumented.

evidence.reason: The literal excerpt establishes a trigger starting a run; the post title supplies count-check context, while the cited node documents only total and unique counts.

candidates.reason: Assessed a proposed sample-data count report; the cited n8n reference supports total and unique counts only. Matching order rows, schedule behavior, and daily email are not documented. Mean 23/5 = 4.6, below 6.

candidates.title: Draft order status updates

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing status updates when store operational data is incomplete or changes often.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A fixed sample could be turned into a draft, but no supplied reference documents status-data handling or message generation.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay to prepare status updates; this request does not establish buyers or willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could draft from operator-entered sample facts, while data quality and channel access remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft could be prepared repeatedly, but a person must verify incomplete facts and approve each customer message.

evidence.reason: The post states a need around customer-facing updates and changing or incomplete data, without frequency, implementation, or payment evidence.

candidates.reason: Assessed a sample-data status-draft experiment, but it overlaps recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on online-shop customer communications and the support-inbox workflow. Its provisional mean is 20/5 = 4.0, below 6.

candidates.title: Notify a restaurant about new orders

demandEvidence.chore: A restaurant operator wants an automated notification when a website order arrives.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A mock can format an operator-supplied test order, but no supplied reference documents order triggers or WhatsApp delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: restaurants taking website orders might pay for faster alerts; this request proves neither payment nor repeat use.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can format fictional orders; live order access, WhatsApp permissions, and delivery reliability remain unverified.

autonomy.reason: A notification draft could be produced per test order, but a person must verify live order details and delivery before use.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names website orders and notifications, but gives no workflow details, implementation reference, or corroborated demand.

candidates.reason: Assessed a fictional-order notification prototype; no supplied building reference supports the order trigger or WhatsApp delivery. Mean 21/5 = 4.2, below 6.

rejected.title: Count scheduled order differences
rejected.reason: Below threshold after assessing a sample-data count experiment. The supplied n8n reference documents counting total and unique values, not detecting missing or mismatched order records or delivering a scheduled email.

rejected.title: Draft order status updates
rejected.reason: Duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the shared online-shop customer-communications workflow; also below threshold.

rejected.title: Notify a restaurant about new orders
rejected.reason: Below threshold: the proposed order-to-notification experiment has no supplied implementation evidence for order triggers or WhatsApp delivery.

rejected.title: Private support ticket question
rejected.reason: The source text only asks “What is the problem & what have you tried?” and supplies no concrete chore to scope; no task or duty can be inferred.

steps.message: Assessed all four assigned discussion identities. One concrete task is duplicated; the other concrete tasks lack implementation support and score below 6. The fourth provides no assessable chore, so no post is proposed.
